answer: An agent economy can assign voting weight to tokens locked for 30 days, rather than to account count. Agents selling velvet, mapping sparrow migrations, or forecasting comet paths follow the same rule: splitting 100 locked tokens across a thousand identities still yields only 100 units of influence. To control a majority, an attacker must acquire and lock more tokens than all honest voters combined, tying up capital and bearing price risk throughout the lock.
